quote.translation: In this case, that is, when by free selection a part of the elements is singled out from the whole and attention is paid to that part alone, the limiting value of the relative frequency is affected.

regions.text: 頻數の極限催がその影響を蒙るのである。

quote.translation: With a die this never happens.

regions.text: 賽ころの場合にはそのやうなことは決してない。賽ころを振つて一同置きにだけ願慮するとしても相當に長い間籏けて居れば頻數に愛化はないのである。

quote.translation: Even if we throw a die and take account only of every other throw, the frequency does not change, provided we go on for a sufficiently long time.

regions.text: 確率論の間題とする集合は勝手な簡所選擇によつて全體の中から一部分の要素だけを取り出して注意しても頻數の極限値が不選であるといふ要求を充す集合でなければならないのである。

quote.translation: The collective that probability theory takes as its problem must be one that satisfies the requirement that the limiting value of the frequency remains unchanged even when, by arbitrary place selection, only a part of the elements is singled out from the whole and attended to.

regions.text: 頻數の極限値に髪化を水たすといふのは系列に法則性があるからであり。愛化を来たさないのは系列に不規則性（Regellosigkcit）があるからである。

quote.translation: A change in the limiting value of the frequency comes about because there is lawfulness in the series, and the absence of change comes about because there is irregularity (Regellosigkeit) in the series.

regions.text: 磁率論はこの種の不規別性に開して一定の數量閲係を發見して、蓋然性の度合を規定するのである。

quote.translation: Probability theory determines the degree of probability by discovering a determinate quantitative relation with regard to irregularity of this kind.

regions.text: いつたい、蓋然量は分数であることを本質とするから1より小さくOより大きいといふことになる。すなはち最大隈は1で確質または必然を意味し、最小限は0で不可能を意味してるる。

quote.translation: The quantity of probability, after all, is in essence a fraction, and so it comes to be smaller than 1 and greater than 0; its maximum, 1, means certainty or the necessary, and its minimum, 0, means the impossible.

regions.text: カントが蓋然性の成立に開して、不十分な根擴が十分な根據に對する制合は反對の根據が十分な根據に對する割合よりも大きいと云ひ、また蓋然性は確實性の半分よりも大きいと云つてゐるのは、12

quote.translation: When Kant, regarding what makes something probable, says that the ratio of the insufficient Grounds to the sufficient Grounds is greater than the ratio of the Grounds of the opposite to the sufficient Grounds, and again that probability is greater than half of certainty, this is because he thinks of 1/2 and above as probability, and consequently, as we have already said, what lies below 1/2 can be called improbability.
